12:01 Local Time, 02:31 GMT, 08:01 IST: What a good toss to lose for Bangladesh. And had Tanzid Tamim taken Steven Smith's catch, things would've been even more rosier. They have Australia four-down after the first session. Hasan Mahmud set the tone early on as he repeatedly troubled Jake Weatherald before he got the left-hander. He then shifted to round the wicket and forced Travis Head to inside-edge one back on. Steven Smith and Marnus tried negotiating a probing spell from the Bangladeshi pacers but the latter fell to Ebadot. Smith should've been caught at 3rd slip and then when Bangladesh were confident that he had nicked it, the review proved otherwise. But in what proved to be the last ball of the session, Green flicked one to mid-wicket and that hands the advantage firmly to Bangladesh. Just the three seamers used and on a wicket which had a bit of nip and movement, they have bowled superbly. Back for the post-lunch session in 35 minutes....

17:32 Local Time, 08:02 GMT, 13:32 IST: Bangladesh find themselves in a very strong position after the opening day of the Test. Cummins won the toss and elected to bat but things didn't go the way he would have hoped. Both Head and Weatherald got off to starts but couldn't capitalise. There was assistance with the new ball for the Bangladeshi seamers and they were on the money. The fact all the ten wickets were bagged by their seamers tells you the story. They picked up four wickets in the first session. There was a promising period for the hosts post lunch as the duo of Smith and Carey batted with composure and assurance. But just after drinks, there was another collapse and that pushed the hosts completely on the back foot. Apart from Smith who made the most of his opportunity (dropped on 2) and went on to score an impressive 71, the others faultered.
